question: What is the primary goal of healthcare waste management in clinical settings?

options.A: To ensure the hospital passes financial audits successfully
options.B: To prevent disease transmission and protect environmental health
options.C: To simplify the daily duties of the cleaning staff
options.D: To reduce the overall operational budget of the hospital

explanation: Effective waste management stops biological and chemical hazards from spreading to staff, patients, and the wider community. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why are nurses considered central to the healthcare waste management system?

options.A: Hospital management legally delegates all waste transportation to nurses
options.B: Nurses generate clinical waste directly during patient care activities
options.C: Ward nurses purchase all color-coded bins used in the facility
options.D: Nurses are solely responsible for incinerating hospital refuse

explanation: Bedside clinical procedures mean nurses handle the initial creation and sorting of medical waste. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h1)

question: What percentage of overall healthcare waste is typically classified as non-hazardous general waste?
explanation: The vast majority of hospital refuse consists of ordinary domestic-type items that do not pose biological risks. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h2)

question: An expired bottle of paracetamol syrup belongs to which category of healthcare waste?
explanation: Unused, expired, or contaminated medications and chemical drugs fall directly under pharmaceutical waste streams. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which infections transmit most frequently through discarded, contaminated injection needles?
explanation: Puncture injuries from unmanaged sharps transfer bloodborne viruses efficiently to unsuspecting individuals. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h3)

question: How does improper healthcare waste disposal commonly trigger cholera outbreaks in a community?

options.A: Leaching medical refuse contaminates local underground water sources used for drinking
options.B: Stray animals eat hazardous waste and transmit rabies to livestock
options.C: Scavengers sell contaminated hospital linen to local restaurant owners
options.D: Infected dust blows from hospital yards into community food markets

explanation: Poorly contained hospital effluents and solid waste seep into water tables, spreading pathogenic waterborne microorganisms. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h3)

question: What toxic compounds are released into the air during open-air burning of PVC plastic medical waste?
explanation: Low-temperature open burning of chlorinated plastics produces dangerous pollutants like dioxins and furans. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h4)

question: A nurse sustains a deep puncture wound on her thumb while attempting to force an overfilled sharps box closed. What hazard does this scenario directly illustrate?
explanation: Overfilling sharps containers violates safety rules and directly exposes healthcare workers to puncture injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h4)

question: At what exact point in the clinical workflow should healthcare waste segregation take place?

options.A: Inside the hospital incinerator room just before burning
options.B: At the point of generation during patient care
options.C: At the municipal landfill site outside the city
options.D: By the waste collection truck driver upon arrival

explanation: Sorting waste immediately where it is produced prevents contamination of non-hazardous items and protects handlers. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why is it strictly prohibited to fill a sharps collection box all the way to the brim?

options.A: Protruding needles increase the risk of accidental puncture injuries to staff
options.B: Plastic boxes crack and leak foul odors when packed tightly
options.C: It makes the box too heavy for the waste truck to lift
options.D: Full boxes cannot fit inside the standard hospital incinerator chamber

explanation: Leaving empty space at the top ensures needles do not poke through or stick out when handling the container. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h5)

question: How should a healthcare worker properly carry a tied infectious waste bag during transport?

options.A: Balanced directly on top of their head
options.B: Clressed tightly against their chest for balance
options.C: Away from the body to prevent injury from stray sharps
options.D: Draped over their bare shoulder like a sack

explanation: Carrying bags away from the body protects staff if needles were improperly placed inside soft bags. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is a mandatory design feature for a temporary healthcare waste storage room?

options.A: Open windows for continuous natural cross-ventilation
options.B: Direct connection to the main hospital cafeteria
options.C: Carpeted flooring to absorb liquid chemical spills
options.D: Secure locks to prevent access by unauthorized persons

explanation: Storage areas must remain locked to keep scavengers, children, and animals away from hazardous biological materials. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h6)

question: What technology does an autoclave use to sterilize infectious healthcare waste?
explanation: Autoclaves utilize pressurized steam to destroy pathogenic microorganisms effectively without open burning. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why are treated sharps and shredded medical waste finally disposed of in engineered landfills?

options.A: To provide nutrients for agricultural crop irrigation
options.B: To prevent environmental contamination and human contact
options.C: To serve as foundation material for building new hospitals
options.D: To encourage recycling by local waste pickers

explanation: Engineered landfills feature protective liners that isolate treated waste from soil and groundwater tables. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h7)

question: Which Nigerian federal agency collaborates in setting environmental guidelines for waste management?
explanation: The Federal Ministry of Environment, alongside health bodies, regulates waste practices to protect public wellbeing. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h8)

question: Which professional action best demonstrates a Nigerian nurse's duty regarding ward waste management?

options.A: Supervising waste segregation and reporting broken safety boxes
options.B: Transporting heavy waste bins outside the hospital unaided
options.C: Leaving all sorting tasks exclusively to junior ward cleaners
options.D: Burning infectious dressings openly behind the ward building

explanation: Nurses oversee clinical environments, ensuring correct segregation and swift reporting of infrastructural faults. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h8)
